summary.title: Debriefing Facilitation Prompts (from The Field Guide To Understanding Human Error)
summary.one_liner: A set of question prompts for facilitating post-incident debriefings, drawn from Sidney Dekker's and Gary Klein's work on understanding how people inside an incident saw the situation.
keywords: field guide to understanding human error
what were you seeing during the incident
takeaways: Structure a debrief around critical junctures in the event sequence, asking what cues people noticed or missed.
Probe the knowledge, prior experience, and expectations participants had when they faced the situation.
Ask about goals, time pressure, options considered, and how the outcome compared with expectations.
Cover communication channels and help-seeking, and reword the questions in the language of the domain.
summary.summary: This handout lists facilitation prompts for debriefing an incident or accident, attributed to Sidney Dekker's Field Guide to Understanding Human Error. It frames the debrief around critical junctures, asking which cues were observed, what knowledge and past experience applied, what expectations people held, and how operational and organizational influences shaped their interpretation. It then gives Gary Klein-style questions covering cues, interpretation, errors, previous experience, goals, taking action, outcome, communications, and help. The page notes that debriefs need not follow the script and that questions should be reformulated in the domain's language.
